# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Formed:** 1761, from western Hampshire County territory
- **County seat:** Pittsfield
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Commonwealth of Massachusetts
- **Geographic note:** Berkshire County is Massachusetts's westernmost county, bordering **both New York and Vermont** — so records for a family near either state line may also exist in adjoining counties across those borders.

---

## A Critical Correction to the Premise

Massachusetts did not begin **centralized, statewide** vital registration until 1841 (Boston excluded until 1850), but it is not accurate to say *nothing civil exists* before that date. Towns were ordered to keep their own local vital records as early as 1639. Compliance was uneven, but a town clerk's birth/marriage/death book may well exist for the family's specific town throughout 1820–1850.

A digitized **"Town Clerk Vital and Town Records"** volume for Berkshire County, 1761–1850 (FamilySearch image group **004500891**, 512 images) was located in this survey. It is **browse-only** — no name index exists, so it must be read page by page.

---

## Church Records

This is the primary avenue for births/baptisms, marriages, and deaths in the pre-1841 window.

| Record Set | Date Range | FamilySearch ID / Image Group | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pittsfield Congregational Church records | 1791–1850 | Image group **004500892** (274 images) | Browse-only images; no name index |
| Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920 (statewide) | 1630–1920 | Collection **1921657** (~988,000 persons) | **Indexed** — searchable by name |

**Research tip:** Because the local Pittsfield Congregational volume is browse-only, also run a name search in the statewide Church Records collection (id 1921657) — it is indexed and may surface the same entries more quickly.

**Coverage gap confirmed:** No tool result in this survey named which other denominations (Baptist, Methodist, Episcopal) kept registers in the border towns of Berkshire County, or whether those registers survive online. That is an access/digitization gap, not evidence such registers never existed.

---

## Cemetery Records

No specific Berkshire County cemetery or sexton register was located online in this survey.

- **Find A Grave** (https://www.findagrave.com/) is a curated resource for cemetery transcriptions and may have volunteer-submitted inscriptions for Berkshire County cemeteries, but no county-specific confirmed holding was returned.
- Physical sexton/burial-ground records, if they survive, would be held locally (town or church office) — no specific office was confirmed by any tool result.

---

## Civil/Town Vital Records (Supplementary)

| Record Set | Date Range | FamilySearch ID / Image Group | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| Berkshire County Town Clerk Vital and Town Records | 1761–1850 | Image group **004500891** (512 images) | Browse-only; no name index |
| Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890 (statewide) | 1620–1890 | Collection **2061550** (~3.5 million persons) | **Indexed** — searchable by name |

---

## Other Supplementary Record Sets

| Collection | FamilySearch Collection ID | Persons | Period |
|---|---|---|---|
| Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991 | 1678901 | ~568,000 | Statewide |
| Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906 | 1459213 | ~346,000 | Statewide |
| Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891 | 1784312 | ~1.2 million | Statewide |

---

## Repository Summary

| Repository | What it holds | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** | Both digitized Berkshire browse-only volumes; indexed statewide church and town vital collections | Free |
| **Find A Grave** | General cemetery transcriptions | Free |
| **Individual town clerk's office** (specific Berkshire border town) | Original town vital/clerk books underlying image group 004500891 | In-person or mail request |
| **Pittsfield Congregational Church / denominational archive** | Original church register underlying image group 004500892 | Contact church or its denominational archive |
| **Berkshire County Probate Court/Registry** | Original probate files | In-person or mail request |

---

## Records NOT Online

- Both digitized Berkshire volumes found (town clerk records and Pittsfield Congregational church records) are **browse-only** with no name index — they must be read image by image.
- No Berkshire-specific cemetery/sexton record was located online.
- No Berkshire-specific land/deed record was located online.
- No confirmed record losses for this county and period were returned; treat these as access and digitization gaps, not destroyed records.

---

## Key Research Tips

1. **Browse both digitized volumes by eye.** Image group 004500891 (town clerk, 1761–1850) and 004500892 (Pittsfield Congregational, 1791–1850) are neither indexed nor full-text searchable. Plan to page through them.

2. **Also search the indexed statewide collections first.** The Massachusetts Church Records collection (1921657) and Town Vital Records collection (2061550) are name-indexed and may surface the family faster than browsing unindexed volumes.

3. **Cross the state lines.** Because the family's town sits near both New York and Vermont, the same family's church, cemetery, and town records may be filed in an adjoining New York or Vermont county. This survey did not confirm the specific neighboring counties; identify the border towns and check those jurisdictions as well.

4. **Town clerk records may predate 1841.** Do not skip the town-level civil record book on the assumption that nothing exists before the statewide act — towns were recording locally throughout this period.

5. **Use probate, naturalization, and passenger lists as supplementary surname searches** once the church or town-clerk browse turns up an approximate date range.

- **Start date:** Town-level recording was ordered from 1639 onward (compliance uneven); statewide centralized registration began in **1841** (Boston excluded until 1850), per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland (c. 1780–1870)

> **Tool note:** The place-search tools could not resolve "Billy," "Bushmills," or "County Antrim" this session, so collection-search and volume-search results are absent below — that is a tool gap, not evidence the records don't exist. The content below is sourced from two FamilySearch Wiki pages retrieved via text search, cited by URL.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, in the barony of Lower Dunluce (partly Carey), poor-law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, Ulster. Contains the post town of **Bushmills** and part of Dunserverick.
- **Former ecclesiastical union:** Billy was head of an union that also included Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride — earlier Church of Ireland administration may have been kept jointly for this group of parishes.
- **Catholic jurisdiction:** forms part of the district of Coleraine.
- **Religious presence on record:** Presbyterian meeting house, Covenanter meeting house, and Wesleyan Methodist meeting house are all noted as present within the parish.

Source: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy#History)

---

## Record Types Available (1780–1870)

### Church Registers *(most critical for an 1825 birth)*
Civil registration of Irish births did not begin until **1864** — your 1825 birth falls entirely in the pre-registration, church-record period.

| Denomination | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Presbyterian** | Confirmed present in parish; register start date **not retrieved** this session | The Billy wiki page has a Presbyterian subsection but it was empty in the page section fetched. The meeting house is confirmed. PRONI and the Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland must be checked directly for the congregation's name and register start date. |
| **Church of Ireland** | Implied by parish structure | No register start date retrieved; check the Billy wiki page and PRONI directly. |
| **Covenanters** | Confirmed meeting house in parish | No register details retrieved. |
| **Wesleyan Methodist** | Confirmed meeting house in parish | No register details retrieved. |
| **Roman Catholic** | Part of Coleraine district | No register start date retrieved. |

**Illustrative pattern from neighboring Ballylinny parish:** Its Presbyterian baptism and marriage registers begin 1837, held originally by the local congregation, with microfilm at PRONI (film MIC 1P/327) and FamilySearch (film 973220). Billy's Presbyterian register likely follows the same custody pattern — but that film number is for Ballylinny, **not** Billy. Source: [Ballylinny Civil Parish, County Antrim — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ballylinny_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy#Church_records)

**Key open gap:** Which specific congregation served Bushmills/Billy (e.g., "First Bushmills," "Ballyreagh," "Dunluce") is **not confirmed** by any tool result this session. Several congregations may have served this small parish.

---

### Civil Registration
- **Non-Catholic marriages:** from 1845
- **All births, marriages, deaths:** from **1864** only
- Nothing for an 1825 birth exists in civil registration.

---

### Census Substitutes
Ireland's 1821–1851 original census returns were largely destroyed (most in the 1922 Four Courts fire), and the 1861 and 1871 returns were officially destroyed after statistical tabulation. The standard substitutes for County Antrim in this era are:

| Record | Period | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **Tithe Applotment Books** | 1820s–1830s | Covers land-occupying heads of household; National Archives of Ireland has online index |
| **Griffith's Valuation** | County Antrim surveyed 1860s | Standard census substitute; searchable at Askaboutireland.ie and PRONI |

No tool result this session confirmed Billy-specific coverage for either — verify directly before relying on them.

---

### Probate Records
- Pre-1858: handled by diocesan/consistorial courts (likely the Diocese of Connor for this area, but unconfirmed by a tool result here).
- Post-1858: civil Probate Registry, typically the District Registry at Londonderry for this part of Antrim.
- No Billy-specific probate holdings confirmed this session.

---

### Land Records
Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation (above) are the main land-occupancy records. Estate rental/lease records for the area (the Giant's Causeway/Bushmills area had notable landed estates) would be in estate papers collections at **PRONI** — not confirmed by a tool result this session.

---

### Immigration/Emigration
Bushmills sits near the Antrim coast with ready access to emigration via Derry/Londonderry and Belfast. This was a heavy Ulster Presbyterian emigration era. No specific passenger-list or emigration record holdings were identified by tool results this session, but this is a productive research avenue.

---

## Key Repositories

| Repository | What to check |
|---|---|
| **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI), Belfast** | Presbyterian and other church register microfilm for Antrim parishes; estate papers; Tithe Applotment books; Griffith's Valuation. Online catalogue at [proni.gov.uk](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/public-record-office-northern-ireland-proni). |
| **Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland, Belfast** | Catalogue of surviving congregation registers; can identify which congregation(s) served Bushmills/Billy and whether a register survives. |
| **FamilySearch Library microfilm** | Microfilm copies of PRONI-held church registers for County Antrim; search the FamilySearch catalog for "Billy" and "Antrim." |
| **National Archives of Ireland / Askaboutireland** | Griffith's Valuation online; Tithe Applotment Books online index. |

---

## Known Record Losses
- **1821–1851 census originals:** largely destroyed (most in 1922).
- **1861 and 1871 census returns:** officially destroyed by government order after statistical use.
- Billy's own church register status is **not yet confirmed** from this survey — treat as "not yet located," not "does not survive."

---

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Go directly to the live Billy wiki page** — the fetched sections were incomplete: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy). Check the Presbyterian and Church of Ireland subsections for register start dates and film numbers.
2. **Search PRONI's online catalogue** for "Billy" and "Bushmills" church registers — the MIC 1P/ series holds most Ulster Presbyterian registers on microfilm.
3. **Contact the Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland** to identify which specific congregation(s) served Billy parish 1780–1870 and whether a register is extant.
4. **Check the ecclesiastical union:** Because Billy was formerly head of a union with Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride, some records may have been kept at the union level rather than parish level.
5. **Search Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation** for Bushmills townlands to find the household by surname in the 1820s–1860s.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland (c. 1780–1870)

**Note on this survey:** the place-resolution tool (`place_search`) returned no match for "Billy," "Bushmills," "County Antrim," "Antrim," or even "Ireland" in this session, and every place-dependent tool chained from it (`collections_search`, `volume_search`, `place_population`, `external_links_search`, a second `catalog_search`) came back empty or with a generic, non-place-specific fallback as a result — these are reported below as unresolved, not as evidence the records don't exist. The FamilySearch Wiki text search, by contrast, did surface genuine content for Billy's own wiki page and a neighboring parish, which is used below and cited by URL.

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Civil parish:** Billy, chiefly in the barony of Lower Dunluce, partly in the barony of Carey, in the poor-law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, province of Ulster. It contains the post town of Bushmills and part of Dunserverick. Source: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy#History).
- **Former ecclesiastical union:** Billy was formerly head of an ecclesiastical union that also comprised the parishes of Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride — meaning earlier Church of Ireland administration for this group of parishes may trace back to Billy. Same source as above.
- **Catholic jurisdiction:** in the Roman Catholic divisions, the parish forms part of the district of Coleraine. Same source.
- **Religious presence:** the same page records meeting houses for Presbyterians, for Covenanters, and for Wesleyan Methodists within the parish — confirming a Presbyterian congregation serving Billy/Bushmills existed, without giving its founding date or register start dates in the portion of the page retrieved.
- **Population/economy/boundary detail:** not returned by any tool this session (place_population could not resolve the place) — treat as unconfirmed rather than absent.

## Boundary changes
No tool result in this session returned boundary-change information specific to Billy parish. Given Ireland's standard 19th-century administrative structure, civil parishes such as Billy sat inside baronies, poor-law unions, and (from 1838) superintendent registrar's districts for civil registration — but no source fetched here confirms any boundary change affecting Billy between 1780 and 1870. This is a gap in this survey, not a statement that none occurred.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
General civil registration of births and deaths in Ireland did not begin until 1864; registration of non-Catholic marriages began earlier (1845), with all marriages from 1864. No Billy-specific or Ireland-specific `{Jurisdiction}_Vital_Records` page was retrievable this session to confirm the exact level and date for this parish — the dates above are general background for Ireland, not sourced to a fetched wiki page for this survey, and should be verified against the General Register Office of Ireland / General Register Office Northern Ireland pages directly. **For the 1825 birth itself, no civil birth registration exists at all** — this falls entirely in the pre-registration, church-record period.

### Church records
This is the central record class for a birth about 1825 in Billy parish, and the one most directly relevant to the Presbyterian question.

- **Presbyterian:** The Billy parish wiki page lists a "Presbyterian" subsection, but the section fetched in this session was an empty heading with no register start date, repository, or film number filled in — [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy, Church records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy#Church_records). This is a real gap in this survey, not evidence no Presbyterian register exists — the page itself confirms a Presbyterian meeting house stood in the parish.
- **By contrast**, the comparable page for the neighboring parish of Ballylinny (further south in County Antrim) does carry filled-in detail: its Presbyterian congregation's baptism and marriage registers begin in 1837, held in original by the local church with microfilm copies at the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI, film MIC 1P/327) and at FamilySearch (film 973220) — [Ballylinny Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ballylinny_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy#Church_records). This is not evidence about Billy's own register start date — it is shown only to illustrate the pattern (local-church custody with PRONI and FamilySearch microfilm copies) that this class of Ulster Presbyterian record typically follows, and to flag that Billy's own equivalent entry needs to be checked directly.
- **Which congregation actually served Bushmills/Billy in 1825 is not confirmed by any tool result in this session** — do not treat "Presbyterian meeting house" in the parish as naming a specific congregation (e.g., "First Bushmills," "Ballyreagh," "Billy Presbyterian Church," "Dunluce") without checking PRONI's and the Presbyterian Historical Society's own catalogues, since several congregations could plausibly have served this small parish and this survey did not pin down which.
- **Church of Ireland:** meeting house/parish church presence is implied by the parish structure, but no register start date was retrieved for Billy.
- **Covenanters and Wesleyan Methodists:** both confirmed present in the parish by the same source, with no register details retrieved.
- **Catholic:** parish forms part of the Coleraine Catholic district per the same source; no register start date retrieved.
- **Language:** English (Ulster-Scots/Irish place-name forms may appear in older entries, but the registers themselves are in English).

### Census records
Ireland's 1821–1851 censuses survive only fragmentarily (most were destroyed), and the 1861 and 1871 originals were destroyed by government order. For County Antrim in this period, the usual substitutes are the **Tithe Applotment Books** (1820s–1830s, pre-Famine land occupiers) and **Griffith's Valuation** (County Antrim surveyed in the 1860s) — standard substitutes for Irish research in this era, but no tool result this session confirmed Billy-specific holdings or digitization for either; this needs direct confirmation at PRONI or FamilySearch's own Ireland census-substitutes pages.

### Probate and court records
No tool result returned Billy- or Antrim-specific probate/court holdings this session. Irish pre-1858 probate was handled by diocesan/consistorial courts (Billy would fall under the relevant Church of Ireland diocese, likely Connor, per the general Ulster pattern — not confirmed by a tool result here); post-1858, by the civil Probate Registry (District Registry at Londonderry for this area is typical but unconfirmed here). Flag as unconfirmed rather than asserting a specific court.

### Land records

Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation (noted above) serve as the land-occupancy record set for this period; estate rental/lease records for the parish (the Giant's Causeway/Bushmills area had notable landed estates) would be held by the relevant estate papers collection, typically at PRONI — not confirmed by a tool result this session.

### Newspaper records

### Immigration/emigration records
Bushmills/Billy sits near the Antrim coast with easy access to emigration via Derry/Londonderry and Belfast; this was a significant emigration era for Ulster Presbyterians. No tool result this session identified specific passenger-list or emigration holdings for this parish — flag as a line of inquiry, not a confirmed source.

Covered above under Land records (Tithe Applotment Books). No separate tax series confirmed by a tool result.

None surfaced by the tools this session.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
No repository/collection row can be built here: `collections_search`, `volume_search`, and `external_links_search` all failed to resolve a standard place for Antrim/Billy/Ireland this session and returned either zero results or a generic, non-place-specific fallback list (U.S. census, Fold3, NARA, a generic FamilySearch Wiki category page, Find A Grave, Newspapers.com) that is not evidence of any actual holding for this parish and should not be cited as such.

**Coverage of this survey:** none of the online-collection tools could be confirmed against this place this session; this is a tool/place-resolution gap, not a finding that no online collections exist. The two repositories named with real content above — PRONI and FamilySearch microfilm — came only from the wiki-text search, for the neighboring Ballylinny parish, cited there as an illustrative pattern only.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI), Belfast | Microfilm/original copies of Presbyterian and other church registers for County Antrim parishes (pattern confirmed for neighboring Ballylinny; not yet confirmed for Billy itself) | In-person or by PRONI's own online catalogue — not checked this session |
| Local Presbyterian congregation (unidentified for Billy/Bushmills) | Original register, where one survives | Contact the specific congregation once identified |

## Records NOT online
Pre-1864 Irish vital events are never in civil registration — they exist only in church registers (where they survive), the tithe/valuation land records, or family sources. This parish's own Presbyterian register entry on the FamilySearch Wiki was empty in this survey, so its existence, survival, and location are unconfirmed from this session's tools — treat that as "not yet located," not "does not survive."

Ireland's earlier 19th-century censuses (1821–1851) were largely destroyed, and the 1861 and 1871 census returns were destroyed by official order after their statistical use — this is a well-known, general loss for all of Ireland, not a Billy-specific finding, and no tool result this session narrowed it to this parish specifically. No tool result confirmed a specific loss or survival for Billy's own church registers; this needs direct confirmation at PRONI.

## Research tips

# Locality Guide: County Cork, Ireland (1830s–1840s)

**Note:** County-level collection searches for Cork did not resolve in this run, so the findings below rest on the Ireland-level FamilySearch Wiki. A follow-up search targeting a specific Cork parish or townland should be run to get more precise details.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Ireland (under British administration in this period)
- **Key events:** The Great Famine began in 1845 (just after your window), triggering mass emigration through Cork ports; the 1922 Four Courts fire later destroyed most pre-1901 Irish government records
- **Denominations:** Predominantly Roman Catholic, with a Church of Ireland (Anglican) minority — both churches kept separate registers held by different custodians

---

## Record Types Available

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **None for this period.** State registration of births, deaths, and Roman Catholic marriages began only on **1 January 1864**; non-Catholic marriages were registered from 1845.
- For the 1830s–1840s, **church registers are the only vital-event source**.

### Church Records
- **Roman Catholic registers** (baptisms and marriages): The **National Library of Ireland** holds free online microfilm/digital images of Catholic registers up to 1880. Survival varies by parish; many Cork parishes' registers begin in the 1810s–1830s.
- **Church of Ireland registers:** Held by the **Representative Church Body Library** and in local custody.
- **Gaps:** Burial records are rarely found in this era. Survival varies widely by parish.

### Census Substitutes (No Usable Census Exists)
Most pre-1901 Irish census returns were destroyed in the 1922 Four Courts fire. The two standard substitutes are:
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Lists occupiers/holders of taxable land — your closest 1830s substitute
- **Griffith's Valuation (early 1850s for Cork):** Lists householders and land occupiers shortly after your target period

Both are available at FamilySearch and the National Archives of Ireland.

### Land Records
The same Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation serve as the primary land records for this period.

### Immigration/Emigration Records
- **Cobh (Queenstown), Cork** was a major Famine-era departure port.
- Passenger manifests list complete family groups including children — always pull the **full manifest**, not just the head of household.

### Other Records
- **Probate/court records:** Many were destroyed in the 1922 fire; treat as a likely loss pending direct confirmation.
- **Newspapers/Cemetery records:** Generic links to Newspapers.com and Find A Grave exist but no Cork-specific collections were confirmed in this run.

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| National Library of Ireland | Catholic parish register images to 1880 | Free online |
| Representative Church Body Library | Church of Ireland parish registers | Contact directly |
| National Archives of Ireland | Tithe Applotment Books, Griffith's Valuation | Online |

---

## Known Record Losses
The **1922 Four Courts fire** destroyed most pre-1901 Irish census returns and many wills and government records — a national-level loss. The Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation are the named substitutes for census research.

---

## Research Tips

1. **Go straight to church registers** — no civil registration exists for the 1830s–1840s. Find your ancestor's parish first, then check the National Library of Ireland for Catholic registers.
2. **Use the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837)** as your closest 1830s census substitute, then Griffith's Valuation (early 1850s) to track the family just after your period.
3. **For emigration:** Pull the full passenger manifest from Cork/Cobh departure records — every family member, including children, is listed.
4. **Identify the specific parish or townland** — Irish research is very parish-dependent, and register start dates and survival vary considerably across County Cork.
5. **Re-run a more targeted search** once you know the specific parish or townland, to identify indexed collection counts and catalog holdings at that level.

---

County Cork in the 1830s–1840s predates Ireland's civil registration system entirely, so there are no government birth, marriage, or death certificates for this era. The core strategy is Roman Catholic or Church of Ireland parish registers (baptisms and marriages), supplemented by the Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation as census substitutes, and passenger manifests if your ancestor emigrated through Cobh. The destruction of most pre-1901 Irish government records in 1922 makes these alternatives essential. Narrowing your research to the specific parish or townland will be the key next step.

# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **Formed:** 1761 — no boundary changes affect the 1820–1850 research window.
- **County seat:** Pittsfield
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Massachusetts
- **Border note:** Berkshire County borders both New York and Vermont. A border-town family may well appear in records on the other side of either state line.

---

## Vital Records (Births, Marriages, Deaths)

**Town-level recording** (1820–1840)
Massachusetts law required towns to record births, marriages, and deaths as early as 1639, though compliance was uneven. For 1820–1840 there is **no centralized state registry** — only the individual town clerk's records. Originals are held by each town/city clerk and can be accessed in person or by written request.

**Statewide recording** (from 1841)
Massachusetts began its first unified statewide system in **1841** (Boston excluded until 1850). From 1841 onward, a parallel state-level record exists alongside the town's.

**Marriage intentions:** Commonly recorded in the bride's home town, with possible additional entries in the groom's home town. For a border family, the "home town" record may actually sit across the line in New York or Vermont.

**What's online:**
| Record | Collection | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890 | FamilySearch collection id 2061550 (~3.46M persons) | Statewide; name-searchable |
| Berkshire town clerk vital & town records, 1761–1850 | FamilySearch image group 004500891 (512 images) | **Browse-only images — no name search** |

---

## Church Records

- **Pittsfield Congregational church records, 1791–1850** — FamilySearch image group 004500892 (274 images); **browse-only, no name search**.
- **Statewide:** "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920" (FamilySearch collection id 1921657, ~988K persons) overlaps this period and is name-searchable.
- Other Berkshire congregations' registers were not confirmed by this survey — a gap in the survey, not evidence they don't exist.

---

## Other Record Types

| Record type | Collection / Repository | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Probate | Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991 (FamilySearch id 1678901, ~568K persons); county probate court | Statewide collection online; original at Berkshire County Probate Court |
| Federal census | Ancestry (U.S. Federal Census) | 1820, 1830, 1840, 1850 all cover this period |
| Passenger lists | Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891 (FamilySearch id 1784312) | Statewide |
| Naturalization | Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906 (FamilySearch id 1459213) | Statewide |
| Military | Fold3 (fold3.com) | No Berkshire-specific holdings confirmed |
| Cemetery | Find A Grave (findagrave.com) | Useful for death/burial data |
| Newspapers | Newspapers.com | Obituaries, marriage notices |
| Land records | Not confirmed online for Berkshire in this survey | Plan for courthouse visit |

---

## Repository Summary

| Repository | Access | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Statewide vital, church, probate, passenger, naturalization collections; two Berkshire-specific browse-only volumes | Free |
| Town/city clerk (per town) | Original vital records | In-person / written request |
| Berkshire County Probate Court | Original probate records | In-person / written request |
| Ancestry | Federal census, some vital | Subscription |
| Find A Grave | Burial records | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Newspaper notices | Subscription |
| Fold3 | Military records | Subscription |

---

## Important Research Tips

1. **Identify the specific town first.** Civil registration is at the town level for the entire 1820–1840 period, so knowing whether your family was in Adams, North Adams, Williamstown, Sheffield, or another Berkshire town is essential before searching vital records.

2. **The two Berkshire-specific digitized volumes are browse-only.** Both the town clerk records (004500891) and the Pittsfield Congregational church records (004500892) must be paged through image by image — plan accordingly.

3. **Check across both state lines.** Because the town is near New York and Vermont, vital, church, and land records for the family may exist in a New York county (Columbia, Rensselaer, Washington) or a Vermont county (Bennington, Rutland) as well.

4. **Massachusetts statewide vital registration starts in 1841.** For events before that year, the town clerk's record is the only official source. The statewide FamilySearch collection (id 2061550) does cover earlier town-recorded events, but completeness depends on what each town submitted.

5. **FamilySearch catalog returned zero hits for Berkshire County** in this survey — a cataloguing gap in the search tool, not proof that no catalog holdings (microfilm, manuscripts) exist. Check the FamilySearch Catalog directly at familysearch.org/search/catalog.

---

**Bottom line:** Start with the statewide FamilySearch vital records collection (id 2061550) for name-searchable coverage, then browse the Berkshire-specific town records volume (004500891) page by page for 1761–1850. For church records, search the statewide church collection (id 1921657) and browse the Pittsfield Congregational volume (004500892) if the family attended that congregation. For 1841 onward, the state-level vital records also apply. And because the family's town sits near two state lines, plan searches in adjacent New York and Vermont counties as well.

## Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

### Jurisdiction Overview
Billy is a civil parish in the barony of Cary, County Antrim, on the north coast of Ireland near Bushmills/the Giant's Causeway coast. This guide covers the period 1780–1870, entirely within the pre-partition era (Northern Ireland was not established until 1921). No population figures could be confirmed through tool lookups for this session.

---

### ⚠️ Coverage Gap Notice
Every place-identification and collection-lookup tool called during this survey returned empty or generic placeholder results for Billy parish, County Antrim, and even "Ireland" broadly. This means:

- **No specific record collections, repositories, or online holdings can be reported as confirmed findings for this parish.**
- Nothing below in the record-availability section can be cited to a tool result from this session.
- General Irish genealogical guidance is provided as background only, not as confirmed findings for Billy specifically.

---

### Record Types for Irish Research in This Period (General Background — Not Confirmed for Billy)

The following record classes are typically relevant for County Antrim parishes in 1780–1870, but their survival and digitization for Billy parish could not be confirmed in this survey:

| Record Type | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Church of Ireland parish registers** | Births/baptisms, marriages, burials |
| **Catholic parish registers** | Often begin later than CoI; variable survival |
| **Civil registration** | Births/deaths from 1864; non-Catholic marriages from 1845; all marriages from 1864 |
| **Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864)** | Land/property valuation; key substitute for census losses |
| **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837)** | Lists landholders obligated to pay tithes |
| **Census fragments** | Most pre-1901 Irish census returns were destroyed; 1831, 1841, 1851 fragments survive in limited form |
| **Probate / estate records** | Wills and administration records |

---

### Repositories (Not Confirmed for Billy This Session)

Likely custodians for original records — but not confirmed by this survey's tools:
- **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)** — primary repository for Antrim records
- **General Register Office for Northern Ireland (GRONI)** — civil registration records
- **Representative Church Body Library** — Church of Ireland registers

---

### Irish Naming Conventions
*Based on the FamilySearch Wiki page **Ireland Naming Customs**, retrieved in this session:*

- **Surname anglicization:** Irish Gaelic surnames were anglicized under English rule, producing variant spellings (e.g., O'Houlihan → Holland). The patronymic prefixes *Mac* ("son of") and *O* ("grandson/descendant of") were frequently dropped or restored, so the same family can appear as O'Flynn, Flynn, or Flinn across records.
- **Spelling was not standardized** — a single family's surname may appear several ways within one parish's own registers.
- **Given names were also anglicized** (e.g., Darby, Dermot, and Jeremiah as variants of one name). Some names (Florence, Sydney, Evelyn) were used for both sexes.
- **Traditional naming pattern** (a clue, not a rule — not universally followed):
  - 1st son → father's father; 2nd son → mother's father; 3rd son → father himself
  - 1st daughter → mother's mother; 2nd daughter → father's mother; 3rd daughter → mother herself
  - A broken pattern is **not** evidence against identity.

---

### Known Record Losses (General Caution)
Most pre-1901 Irish census returns were destroyed (the 1922 Four Courts fire and earlier deliberate destruction). This is a well-known caution for Irish research broadly, but was not confirmed by any tool result this session as specifically tied to Billy parish.

---

To complete this locality guide with confirmed record-availability findings for Billy parish, re-run the survey with a working place-lookup for the civil parish/barony/county mapping, or supply that mapping directly to allow the collection and repository searches to resolve correctly.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim (Bushmills area), 1780–1870

## Jurisdiction Overview
Billy is a civil parish of ancient origin in County Antrim, Province of Ulster, centered on the village of Bushmills on the north Antrim coast near the Giant's Causeway. After the partition of Ireland in 1921–22, it falls within Northern Ireland (United Kingdom). The area was predominantly Church of Ireland (Anglican) and Presbyterian, with a Catholic minority — broadly typical of County Antrim.

The single most significant event for record availability in this period is the **1922 Public Record Office of Ireland fire in Dublin**, which destroyed approximately two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers nationally.

---

## Record Types Available

### Church Records — Including Church of Ireland Registers
Church registers are the **primary source** for the entire 1780–1870 window, as civil registration did not begin until 1864 (non-Catholic marriages from 1845).

- **Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopalian):** The dominant denomination in County Antrim. Record-keeping began as early as 1536 nationally, but roughly two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in the 1922 fire. **Whether Billy parish's own registers survived is not confirmed in this survey.** This must be verified directly with the repositories listed below.
- **Presbyterian:** Very strong in County Antrim. Presbyterian registers frequently survive and are often held at PRONI.
- **Roman Catholic:** Also present in the area; Catholic registers were generally held locally and many survived 1922.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, and burials (burial registers are less common for Catholic/Presbyterian congregations).
- **Language:** English.

### Civil Registration
- **Births, marriages, deaths:** General civil registration began **1 January 1864**. Non-Catholic marriages were registered from **1 April 1845**.
- These cover only the last years of the 1780–1870 window.
- **Post-1922 custodian:** General Register Office (Northern Ireland), Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Belfast.

### Census Records
Ireland's pre-1901 censuses (1821, 1831, 1841, 1851) were almost entirely destroyed — by government order or in the 1922 fire. No confirmed surviving fragments for Billy/Antrim were identified in this survey. The 1901 and 1911 censuses (outside this window) are fully available online.

### Land Records
Land records are the most useful census substitute for this period:
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (c.1856–1864):** Records every landowner and occupier in Ireland — County Antrim was surveyed in this period. Available online (AskAboutIreland.ie and other sites).
- **Tithe Applotment Books (c.1823–1837):** Lists landholders who paid tithes to the Church of Ireland. County Antrim coverage exists; available online via NAI and IrishGenealogy.ie.

### Probate Records
Pre-1858 probate was handled by diocesan church courts and is heavily affected by 1922 fire losses. Post-1858 probate moved to civil registries. County Antrim falls under the Armagh/Down ecclesiastical district.

### Other Record Types
- **Military records, newspapers, cemetery records, immigration/emigration lists:** Not confirmed in this session. County Antrim (including the Bushmills area) was a major source of Ulster emigration to North America in this period — passenger and port records may supplement church records.

---

## Repository Guide

### Physical Repositories

| Repository | Relevant Holdings | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Church of Ireland RCB Library**, Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14 D14 N735 | Surviving CoI parish registers; **List of Parish Registers** finding aid (shows what survived and where it's held) | +353 (0)1 492 3979; library@ireland.anglican.org |
| **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)**, 2 Titanic Boulevard, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Church records (originals & microfilm) for NI parishes; Guide to Church Records PDF; some digitized records | 028 9053 4800; proni@communities-ni.gov.uk |
| **General Register Office (Northern Ireland)** | Civil births, marriages, deaths from 1845/1864 | Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Belfast |
| **National Archives of Ireland**, Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 | Tithe Applotment Books, pre-partition genealogy records | mail@nationalarchives.ie |

### Online Sources

| Site | What It Holds | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **IrishGenealogy.ie** | CoI & Catholic registers, civil registration indexes | Free |
| **AskAboutIreland.ie** | Griffith's Valuation digitized | Free |
| **RootsIreland.ie** | Indexed Irish parish records | Subscription |
| **FindMyPast / Ancestry** | Ffolliott Collection (CoI baptisms/marriages/burials); Diocesan & Prerogative Marriage License Bond Indexes 1623–1866 | Subscription |

---

## Key Known Record Losses
- Approx. **two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers** destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire.
- Pre-1901 **census records** almost entirely destroyed.
- Many **pre-1858 probate records** lost in the same fire.

---

## Research Tips
1. **First step:** Check the **RCB Library's List of Parish Registers** PDF (linked from the FamilySearch Ireland Church Records Wiki page) to find out definitively whether Billy parish's Church of Ireland registers survived 1922 and what years they cover.
2. **Contact PRONI** directly for its Guide to Church Records, which lists by civil parish which churches existed and whether PRONI holds copies.
3. Even if the family was **not** Church of Ireland, search CoI registers — it was the state-established church and recorded many events.
4. **Presbyterian registers** in County Antrim frequently survive and are often at PRONI — a valuable alternative if CoI registers were lost.
5. Use **substitute indexes** for lost registers: the Ffolliott Collection and Diocesan/Prerogative Marriage License Bonds.
6. **Griffith's Valuation** (c.1856–64) and the **Tithe Applotment Books** (c.1823–37) serve as census substitutes and can help place families in this parish during the target period.
7. Because civil/Catholic parish boundaries may differ from civil parish boundaries, also search neighboring parishes if expected registers are silent.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **Baronies:** Carey and Lower Dunlune; poor law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, Ulster.
- **Post town / settlements:** Bushmills; part of Dunserverick.
- **Religious denominations present:** Church of Ireland, Roman Catholic (district of Coleraine), Presbyterian, Covenanter, Wesleyan Methodist.
- **Post-1922:** County Antrim, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom — records may be catalogued under either the pre- or post-partition place name.

---

## Civil Registration — Start Dates
| Event type | Registration began |
|---|---|
| Protestant marriages | 1845 |
| All marriages / births / deaths | 1864 |

For virtually the **entire 1780–1870 window**, civil registration did not exist. Church registers are the **only vital-event source** until 1864.

---

## Digitized Records Found (confirmed by tools)

| Record | Coverage | FamilySearch Image Group | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ballylinny, Billy — Christenings | 1837–1868 | 007907410_008_M9VF-SK5 (65 images) | Full-text searchable; not name-indexed |
| Ballylinny, Billy — Marriages | 1837–1864 | 007765074_009_M9VX-Q7W (50 images) | Full-text searchable; not name-indexed |
| Ballylinny, Billy — Valuation | 1867–1881 | 004689599 | Browse only |
| Deffrick National School Girls | 1867–1933 | 008682995_005_M94W-68Y | Browse only |

**Coverage gap confirmed:** No digitized church register for Billy parish itself (Church of Ireland, Catholic, Covenanter, or Methodist) was found in FamilySearch's catalog, collections index, or volume search for this period. The two Ballylinny volumes start only in 1837, leaving 1780–1836 entirely uncovered online.

---

## Repository Guide — Closing the Church-Register Coverage Gap

### Online Repositories

| Repository | What it fills | URL / Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** | Ballylinny volumes above (browse free) | https://www.familysearch.org |
| **PRONI Church Records Guide** | Authoritative list of which Billy-area registers survive and where — the essential next step | https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf |
| **PRONI Digitised Church Records** | On-site/online church-record images for Northern Ireland | https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni |
| **NLI Catholic Parish Registers** | Catholic baptism/marriage registers, free online | https://registers.nli.ie/ |
| **RCB Library Parish Register List** | Church of Ireland — confirms survival and location of Billy CoI register | https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf |
| **RootsIreland.ie** | General Irish parish-register index (subscription) | https://www.rootsireland.ie |
| **Ulster Historical Foundation** | Large Ulster-wide church-record database | https://www.ancestryireland.com |
| **FindMyPast — Ffolliott Collection & Betham Abstracts** | CoI baptism/marriage/burial indexes; pre-1922 abstracts | https://www.findmypast.com |

### Physical Repositories

| Repository | Address | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI** (primary Northern Ireland archive) | 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ | proni@communities-ni.gov.uk · 028 9053 4800 |
| **RCB Library** (Church of Ireland) | Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735 | library@ireland.anglican.org · +353 (0)1 492 3979 |
| **National Archives of Ireland** | Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 | mail@nationalarchives.ie |

---

## Land Records (useful when vital records are absent)
- **Tithe Applotment Books** (1820s) — applicable to Billy parish; confirmed by FamilySearch Wiki.
- **Griffith's Valuation** (1840s) — applicable; Ballylinny valuation volume 1867–1881 found digitized.

---

## Known Record Losses
- **Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers nationally were destroyed in 1922** (Public Record Office of Ireland fire). Whether Billy parish's CoI register survived is **not confirmed** — PRONI and the RCB Library are the authorities to contact.
- No tool result confirmed loss or survival of Billy's Catholic, Presbyterian, Covenanter, or Methodist registers specifically.

---

## Research Tips
1. **1780–1836 is entirely uncovered online** — pursue PRONI and the RCB Library directly for any register pre-dating the Ballylinny volumes.
2. Catholic and Presbyterian registers **rarely include burials** — a missing burial entry does not indicate denomination.
3. **Catholic parish boundaries ≠ civil parish boundaries** — search surrounding parishes if nothing is found in Billy.
4. Search Church of Ireland records even for non-CoI families; they sometimes recorded neighbours.
5. Use both pre-1922 ("Billy, County Antrim, Ireland") and post-1922 ("Billy, County Antrim, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom") place names when searching catalogs.
6. Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation can substitute for missing vital records across much of the period.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780-1870)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Ancient civil parish; partly in the barony of Carey, but chiefly in the barony of Lower Dunluce, poor law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, province of Ulster (per the FamilySearch Wiki's Billy Civil Parish page: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy).
- **County seat / administrative center:** The parish contains the post town of Bushmills and part of Dunserverick; the parish was formerly head of an ecclesiastical union also comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride, together forming the corps of the archdeaconry of Connor (same page).
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Ireland (pre-1922); after 1922, County Antrim, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom.
- **Population during period:** This survey could not retrieve population figures for Billy parish — `place_population` returned no data for this standard place.
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (part of the district of Coleraine), Presbyterian, Covenanter, and Wesleyan Methodist meeting houses, and the Church of Ireland parish church (same FamilySearch Wiki page). No denomination's start date for registers in Billy itself is given by that page.
- **Key historical events:** None stated by the retrieved tool results for this specific parish and period.

## Boundary changes
- The FamilySearch Wiki's parish page does not describe any boundary change to Billy civil parish during 1780-1870. `place_search` shows the parish's standard-place label changing only with the 1922 partition (pre-1922: "Billy, County Antrim, Ireland"; post-1922: "Billy, County Antrim, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom") — a jurisdictional relabeling, not a change in the parish's own boundaries. Records from before 1922 should be sought under the pre-partition name/catalog entries as well as the post-1922 ones, since catalogers use both.

## Available record types

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of Ireland, Roman Catholic, Presbyterian, Covenanter, and Wesleyan Methodist (per the parish's Wiki page). The parish-level Wiki article lists subsection headings for Catholic, Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Methodist, Society of Friends, and "Others," but every one of those subsections is empty of content — the page states no start dates or holdings for Billy's own registers.
- **Record types:** Baptism, marriage, and burial registers are the principal Irish church record types generally (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records); that page notes Catholic and Presbyterian registers frequently lack burial registers.
- **Where held — confirmed by tool results:** `volume_search` found two digitized FamilySearch image groups specifically for **Ballylinny, Billy, County Antrim** (a townland within the parish area returned under this search): christenings 1837-1868 (imageGroupNumber 007907410_008_M9VF-SK5, 65 images, full-text searchable, not name-indexed) and marriages 1837-1864 (imageGroupNumber 007765074_009_M9VX-Q7W, 50 images, full-text searchable, not name-indexed). Both are in English.
- **Gap:** No church register for Billy parish itself (as opposed to the Ballylinny volumes) was returned by `volume_search`, `collections_search` (0 results), or `catalog_search` (0 hits) for 1780-1870. This is a confirmed digitization/cataloging gap for this specific parish in this tool run, not evidence the registers do not exist — see Repository guide below for where to pursue this gap directly.
- **Language:** English.

### Civil registration (vital records)
- **Start date:** Per the parish's own FamilySearch Wiki page: state civil registration of **births and deaths began in 1864**; registration of **Protestant marriages began in 1845**, with **all marriages registered by 1864** (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy). For most of the 1780-1870 target window, civil registration did not exist (pre-1864 for births/deaths, pre-1845/1864 for marriages), so church registers are the primary source for the bulk of the period.
- **Where held:** General Register Office (Northern Ireland), GRONI, for post-1864/1845 events; see Ireland Civil Registration page.

### Census records
- No national census survives for 1780-1870 Ireland in usable household form for this period (1821-1851 censuses were largely destroyed; 1861/1871 originals were destroyed by government order) — this survey did not independently confirm Billy-specific losses; see Known record losses below for what is and is not confirmed.

### Probate and court records
- The Billy parish Wiki page points to the general `Ireland_Probate_Records` article; no parish-specific probate holdings were returned by this survey's tool calls.

### Land records
- **Types:** Griffith's Valuation (property valuation for tax, begun in the 1840s by Richard Griffith) and Tithe Applotment Books (a tax paid to the church, begun in the 1820s) are named on the parish's own Wiki page as applicable to Billy.
- **Confirmed by volume_search:** A Valuation record for Ballylinny, Billy, 1867-1881 (imageGroupNumber 004689599, volume "VAL 12B/1/7B," 76 images, browse-only, not full-text searchable).

### School records
- **Confirmed by volume_search:** Deffrick National School Girls register, Billy parish, Apr 1867-Sep 1933 (imageGroupNumber 008682995_005_M94W-68Y, 50 images, browse-only).

### Military, cemetery, newspaper, immigration/emigration, tax records

General Ireland-level pointers exist on the FamilySearch Wiki (Ireland Military Records, Cemeteries, Newspapers, Emigration & Immigration, Taxation) but were not individually fetched in this run; treat each as a gap pending a dedicated check.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840s–1860s)

## Jurisdiction Overview
Schuylkill County was an established jurisdiction throughout this period, formed in 1811 as a Pennsylvania county. It remained a stable jurisdiction with no confirmed boundary changes during the 1840s–1860s target window.

---

## Available Record Types

### Church Records
- **Lutheran Church Records (1840–1875)** — FamilySearch image group 004288771, 198 images, written in both English and German.
- ⚠️ **Not name-indexed, not full-text searchable** — must be browsed image by image. Researchers must be prepared to read German-language entries.

### Census Records
- **U.S. Federal Census (1850–1860)** — FamilySearch image group 007621224, 412 images, **96% name-indexed and full-text searchable**. Also available via Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/).
- The **1840 census** for Schuylkill County was **not confirmed** as digitized in this survey.

### Probate Records
- **Probate Records (1845–1880)** — FamilySearch image group 004812990, 286 images. Only 4% name-indexed, but **full-text searchable** — search by text rather than name index.
- Also covered (statewide) by FamilySearch collection 1999196, "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994."

### Tax Records (Background Only)
- Ancestry's "Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768–1801" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) predates the target period — useful for background context only.

---

## Records NOT Confirmed Online for This Period
The following **were not found in any online collection** during this survey — their absence reflects a digitization gap, not necessarily that they don't exist:
- **Land records**
- **Military records** (Mexican-American War, Civil War)
- **Cemetery records**
- **Newspaper records**
- **Immigration/naturalization records**
- **Vital records (civil registration)** — Pennsylvania's statewide registration start date could not be confirmed; church records are the primary substitute.

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | What's Available | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Federal Census 1850–1860 (indexed); Probate Records 1845–1880 (full-text); Lutheran Church Records 1840–1875 (browse-only) | Free |
| Ancestry | 1850 U.S. Federal Census – Schuylkill County | Subscription |

No physical repositories (courthouse, state archive, historical society) were returned by tools in this survey. FamilySearch's Catalog returned zero hits for Schuylkill County — this is a cataloguing gap, not proof that no physical holdings exist.

---

## Known Record Losses
No tool result reported any destroyed or lost record set for Schuylkill County. None should be assumed destroyed.

---

## Research Tips
1. **Census first:** The 1850 and 1860 federal censuses are well-indexed — start here for locating individuals and households.
2. **Probate:** Full-text search the digitized probate volume (1845–1880) even though it lacks a name index.
3. **Church records:** The Lutheran volume (1840–1875) has no index — plan to browse it page by page, and be prepared for German-language entries.
4. **Vital records:** Because Pennsylvania's civil registration start date is unconfirmed, treat church records as your primary source for births, marriages, and deaths throughout this entire period.
5. **FamilySearch Catalog:** The catalog returned zero hits through this survey's tool — consider searching the catalog manually at FamilySearch.org by county name for additional holdings.
6. **Physical repositories:** Records not yet digitized (land, military, cemetery, newspapers) likely exist in physical form at the county courthouse or a Pennsylvania historical society; these repositories could not be confirmed by name in this survey.

---

*Survey note: FamilySearch Research Wiki pages consulted during this survey returned only generic, non-Pennsylvania-specific content, so dates for official civil registration and other Pennsylvania-specific details remain unconfirmed. A targeted follow-up on Pennsylvania's vital-record registration history is recommended.*

# Locality Guide: Christ Church Philadelphia Marriage Register (1734)

## Short Answer

The original 1734 Christ Church marriage register is held by **Christ Church, Philadelphia itself** — an active Episcopal/Anglican congregation. To see the original (not a transcription), you must contact the church directly.

---

## Why the Church, Not an Archive?

According to the FamilySearch Research Wiki's *Pennsylvania Church Records* page, the **Diocese of Pennsylvania** only holds records for *closed* Episcopal parishes. Christ Church is an active parish, so its original registers remain in the church's own custody — they are not held by the diocese or any other repository.

---

## What Is (and Is Not) Online

| Repository | What It Holds | Is It the Original? |
|---|---|---|
| **Historical Society of Pennsylvania (HSP)** | *Abstracts* (derivatives) drawn from Pennsylvania church records — marriage abstracts cover 1512–1989 | ❌ No — explicitly described as abstracts, not originals |
| **FamilySearch** | Pennsylvania Compiled Marriages 1700–1900; Pennsylvania Civil Marriages 1677–1950 | ❌ No — compiled/derivative indexes |
| **FamilySearch Catalog** | Search for "Christ Church marriages, Philadelphia" returned **0 hits** | No digitized original found |
| **Christ Church, Philadelphia** | The original registers, per the FamilySearch Wiki | ✅ Yes — this is where to go |

No digitized or microfilmed copy of this specific 1734 marriage register was found in any search conducted during this survey.

---

## Known Losses

None reported. The absence from FamilySearch's catalog reflects a digitization gap — not evidence that the register was destroyed.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Contact Christ Church, Philadelphia directly** to inquire about viewing or obtaining access to the original 1734 marriage register. The FamilySearch Wiki identifies this as the correct access route for an active parish.
2. If you only need a derivative record for research purposes, the **HSP marriage abstracts** (available in-person at HSP or through FamilySearch) cover 1734 and may contain an entry for the marriage you're researching — just be aware it is an abstract, not the original register page.
3. Check **HSP's own finding aids** for any published transcription of Christ Church's early records (some exist in genealogical literature), though the survey found no such FamilySearch-catalogued edition.

# Locality Guide: Alabama Region, United States (c. 1798–1819, before statehood)

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **Mississippi Territory (1798–1817):** The area that became Alabama was part of Mississippi Territory before splitting off as Alabama Territory (1817–1819), then achieving statehood in 1819.
- **Earlier administrations:** Spain, Britain, and France had administered parts of the Mobile area before U.S. control. Each left distinct record types in different archives.

## Boundary Changes
- Before 1798: Spanish, British, and French colonial administration (especially Mobile area)
- 1798–1817: Mississippi Territory
- 1817–1819: Alabama Territory (split from Mississippi Territory)
- 1819: Alabama statehood

**Research implication:** Search under "Mississippi Territory" for events before 1817, then "Alabama Territory" for 1817–1819 — these are successive labels for the same place, not separate jurisdictions.

---

## Available Record Types

### Church Records
- **FamilySearch collection:** "Alabama, Church Records, 1803–1950" (id 1986396, ~156,789 persons) — overlaps the target period from 1803.
- **Spanish-era Mobile records:** Spanish-period church registers of the Mobile District are held at the **Archivo General de Indias, Seville**, with copies at the **Library of Congress**.
- No civil vital registration existed during this territorial period; church records are the primary substitute for births, marriages, and deaths.

### Census Records
- **Territorial censuses:** Mississippi Territory conducted censuses in **1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810** that included present-day Alabama — held at the **Alabama Department of Archives and History, Montgomery**.
- **Compiled online index:** "Alabama, Compiled Census and Census Substitutes Index, 1810–1890" (id 2016756, ~287,634 persons) on FamilySearch.
- No federal census covered this region before 1820.

### Marriage Records
- **FamilySearch collection:** "Alabama, County Marriages, 1809–1950" (id 1598408, ~1,224,690 persons) — covers the late territorial period from 1809.

### Probate & Court Records
- **FamilySearch collection:** "Alabama, Probate Records, 1809–1985" (id 1537764, ~438,210 persons).
- **Digitized but unindexed (browse-only):**
  - Territorial court and land records, Alabama, 1808–1819 (imageGroupNumber 004512889, 214 images, 0% indexed)
  - County deed and probate records, Washington, Alabama, 1803–1820 (imageGroupNumber 004512890, 96 images, 0% indexed)
  - Both must be browsed image by image — no name search is possible.

### Land Records
- Spanish, British, and French colonial land grants predate U.S. control in the Mobile area.
- U.S. territorial land matters appear in the browse-only territorial court/land records volume (004512889, 1808–1819) listed above.

### Colonial Records (French)
- French colonial Mobile records (1702–1763) are held at the **Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer, Aix-en-Provence**, with microfilm copies at the **Mobile Municipal Archives**.

### Record Types Not Confirmed Online for This Period
- Military records, tax records, newspaper archives, immigration records, and cemetery records were not confirmed by any tool for this specific place and time. Their absence online should not be taken as evidence they don't exist — plan to contact physical repositories.

---

## Repository Guide

### Online
| Repository | Key Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Church records (1803+), county marriages (1809+), probate records (1809+), census substitute index (1810+), two browse-only unindexed territorial volumes | Free |

### Physical
| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| **Alabama Department of Archives and History, Montgomery** | Mississippi Territory censuses 1801, 1805, 1808, 1810; additional territorial records |
| **Archivo General de Indias, Seville** | Spanish-period Mobile District church registers, census returns, land grants; copies at Library of Congress |
| **Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer, Aix-en-Provence** | French colonial Mobile records, 1702–1763; microfilm copies at Mobile Municipal Archives |
| **Mobile Municipal Archives** | Microfilm of French colonial records |

---

## Key Research Tips

1. **Search the two territorial periods separately:** Mississippi Territory (before 1817) and Alabama Territory (1817–1819) are both needed for complete coverage.
2. **Budget time to browse unindexed images:** The two FamilySearch digitized volumes for 1803–1820 are 0% name-indexed and cannot be searched by name — you must page through them.
3. **No civil vital registration exists** for this period; prioritize church records, probate records, and territorial censuses as birth/marriage/death substitutes.
4. **Oldest Mobile-area records sit in overseas archives** (Spain and France) — written requests or in-person visits, or checking for Library of Congress / Mobile Municipal Archives copies, will be necessary.
5. **FamilySearch Catalog** returned no hits for Alabama in this period — this is a cataloguing gap, not proof no holdings exist. Consult the Alabama Department of Archives and History's own catalog directly.

- **Economy / ethnic composition / religious denominations:** Not confirmable from tool results this run; a `wiki_search` result notes the Creek and Cherokee nations occupied much of the territory and that Spanish, British, and French colonial administrations preceded U.S. control around Mobile.
- **Key historical events:** Mississippi Territory organized 1798; Alabama Territory split off 1817; statehood 1819 (Wikipedia, "Alabama," https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama).

## Boundary changes
- Before 1798: claimed/administered in parts by Spain, Britain, and France (Mobile area).
- 1798–1817: part of Mississippi Territory.
- 1817–1819: part of Alabama Territory (split from Mississippi Territory, which became the state of Mississippi in 1817).
- 1819: Alabama statehood.
- This is a temporal succession, not a geographic split — records for an ancestor in the Alabama region before 1817 should be sought under "Mississippi Territory," and 1817–1819 under "Alabama Territory," as one continuous research trail rather than unrelated jurisdictions.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

Statewide civil registration in Alabama is generally known to begin in the 20th century, but this guide does not state a year because no tool result for this place/period confirmed one.
- **What exists / where held:** No civil vital registration existed in this territorial period; see Church records and Probate/Court records below for substitute sources.

### Church records
- **What's documented:** `collections_search` found "Alabama, Church Records, 1803–1950" (collection id 1986396, ~156,789 persons) — overlaps the target period from 1803.

## Repository guide

### Physical repositories

| Mobile Municipal Archives | Microfilm copies of French colonial records | In-person or written request |

Treat the record-type findings above (from `wiki_search`, `collections_search`, `volume_search`, and `catalog_search`) as the reliable basis for this guide, and re-run the Wiki lookups later for narrative/registration-date detail.
- `catalog_search` for "Alabama, United States" returned zero hits — this is a cataloguing gap for the FamilySearch Catalog specifically, not evidence that no microfilm or manuscript holdings exist; consult the Alabama Department of Archives and History's own catalog directly.

- The two digitized volumes found (territorial court/land records, and Washington County deed/probate records) are both 0% indexed and not full-text searchable — budget time to browse them image by image rather than searching by name.

This survey covers the region that became Alabama from about 1798 to 1819, back when it was first part of the Mississippi Territory and then the short-lived Alabama Territory, before statehood. Surviving records from that era are scattered: territorial censuses from 1801–1810 and probate and court papers are held by the Alabama Department of Archives and History in Montgomery, some are digitized on FamilySearch but only as unindexed images that must be browsed page by page, and the oldest material from the Mobile area (while it was under Spanish and French rule) is held overseas in Spanish and French national archives, with some copies at the Library of Congress and in Mobile. # Locality Guide: Arkansas Post / Spanish Arkansas (to 1800)

## Jurisdiction Overview

Arkansas Post was established by the French in 1686 and lay in the lower Mississippi Valley. After the 1763 Treaty of Paris, Spain administered the territory until secretly retroceding it to France in 1800; the 1803 Louisiana Purchase then brought it under the United States. It was the sole organized settlement and seat of civil/military authority in this period. Under Spain, it fell within the Spanish Louisiana administration, governed from New Orleans/St. Louis (Upper Louisiana). FamilySearch's place system only recognizes "Arkansas, United States" from 1836 onward, so colonial-era materials require targeted searching by the historic name "Arkansas Post."

---

## Available Record Types

### Church Records *(primary vital-records source)*
- **Denominations:** Roman Catholic (French missionaries from the early 1700s, continuing under Spanish administration)
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, and burials — these functioned as the vital records of the period
- **FamilySearch digitized volume:** Image group **008814402**, 64 images, "Sacramental Registers (Spanish Colonial)," Arkansas Post, **1763–1800**, in **Spanish**
  - ⚠️ **0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable** — browse-only, image by image; reading Spanish is required
- **Physical repositories:** Roman Catholic Diocese of Little Rock (original or earliest registers); Arkansas History Commission (transcribed copies)
- **Language:** Spanish; earlier French-era entries may be in French

### Census Records (Padrones)
- No U.S. federal census applied here — Arkansas fell outside the 1790–1800 federal census
- Spain kept colonial censuses ("**padrones**") at the post, described in the FamilySearch Wiki
- **Where held:** Arkansas History Commission (Little Rock), Archivo General de Indias (Seville, Spain), and on microfilm at the Library of Congress
- **Status:** Not digitized or indexed online — physical/archival access only

### Land Records
- Spanish administration issued land concessions recorded in the colonial papers
- **Date range:** 1763–1800
- **Where held:** Arkansas History Commission / Archivo General de Indias / Library of Congress microfilm
- Not confirmed available online in any tool result

### Military Records
- Arkansas Post was a Spanish military installation; no service or muster records for this period were located in this survey
- General U.S. military repositories (NARA) do not hold Spanish colonial military records

### Probate / Notarial Records
- Spanish colonial administration generally generated notarial and judicial records, but none specific to Arkansas Post surfaced in this survey

---

## Repository Guide

### Online
| Repository | Collection | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Vol. 008814402 — Sacramental Registers (Spanish Colonial), 1763–1800 | Browse-only; Spanish; 64 images; no name index |

### Physical / Archival
| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| **Arkansas History Commission** (Little Rock, AR) | Transcribed Spanish colonial censuses, land concessions, church register transcripts |
| **Archivo General de Indias** (Seville, Spain) | Original Spanish colonial administrative records (censuses, land concessions, correspondence) |
| **Library of Congress** | Microfilm of the colonial records described above |
| **Roman Catholic Diocese of Little Rock** | Original (or earliest surviving) sacramental registers for Arkansas Post |

---

## Coverage Gaps Found in This Survey
- `collections_search` returned 3 Arkansas collections, but all three (county marriages 1837–1957, Freedmen's Bureau 1865–1872, census substitutes 1819–1870) post-date 1800 — a real gap in online coverage for the colonial era
- `catalog_search` for "Arkansas, United States" returned **0 hits** — treat this as a cataloguing gap, not evidence the records don't exist
- Spanish colonial censuses, land concessions, and military records were **not located as online/digitized resources** in this survey

---

## Research Tips

1. **Browse the sacramental register image by image.** Volume 008814402 on FamilySearch (1763–1800) has no name index — you must work through all 64 images, and you will need reading knowledge of Spanish or paleography assistance.

2. **Search by historic name, not the modern state.** FamilySearch's place system only resolves "Arkansas, United States" from 1836; searching by that standardized place will miss colonial materials. Use "Arkansas Post" directly.

3. **Contact the Arkansas History Commission directly** for colonial padrones and land concessions — these are described in the FamilySearch Wiki as held there but are not online.

4. **Consider the Archivo General de Indias (Seville)** for original Spanish colonial records, or the Library of Congress for microfilm copies of those holdings.

5. **Write to the Diocese of Little Rock** for original sacramental register access or guidance on additional register survival.

---

*This survey found one digitized FamilySearch volume covering the Spanish colonial period. The colonial census (padrón) and land-concession records described by the FamilySearch Wiki exist but are held only in physical repositories — Arkansas History Commission, the Spanish national archive in Seville, and on Library of Congress microfilm — and are not confirmed online. A research plan built around browsing the sacramental register and writing to the physical repositories would be the recommended next step.*
